job.style: a conversation between a teacher and two students

response.passage: In a classroom in Bengaluru, Mr. Sharma held up a plastic bottle. 'Students, plastic pollution is a growing crisis,' he said. Rohan asked, 'Sir, why does plastic end up in our rivers?' Mr. Sharma replied, 'It happens because people throw waste into drains, which then flow into the water bodies.' Meera added, 'I saw a news report about 500 turtles being affected by plastic in the ocean last year.' Mr. Sharma nodded, 'That is true, Meera. In 2022, scientists found that microplastics are now everywhere. Even in the Himalayas, plastic waste is found because humans leave trash behind during treks.' Rohan looked worried. 'Does that mean all plastic is bad?' Mr. Sharma smiled gently. 'Not exactly. Plastic is a material, but our habit of throwing it away is the problem. Think of it as a tool that we misuse.' Meera sighed, 'I will tell my brother to stop using plastic bags.' Mr. Sharma concluded, 'Good, small steps matter. If we reduce our usage, we can protect our beautiful country.'
response.summary: Mr. Sharma explains to his students that plastic pollution is a serious issue caused by human waste. He clarifies that while plastic is a useful material, our habit of littering is what causes environmental damage.
